text: In the candlelit stacks of the Quillfeather Archive, curators still speak of Rosalind Tavner as the institution’s unlikely founder, a scholar-broker who began collecting provincial ledgers and private correspondence in 1987 after the mill closures stripped Northfold of its memorykeepers. Tavner, then a lecturer at Mirebank College, used a single rent-controlled room on Lark Street to preserve church rolls, shipping manifests and the diaries of trade families, insisting that “a town’s future depends on its paper past.” The archive was formally incorporated in 1994, when donations swelled its shelves to 18,000 items. Today, its trustees credit Tavner’s stubbornness with creating the region’s most consulted historical repository, one that still carries her original brass filing tags.
